statement: A surety who assumes liability as 'surety and co-principal debtor' waives the benefit of excussion.
supporting_quote: These special defenses protected sureties against possible collusion between the debtor and the creditor. By way of clause 14, the guarantors have renounced all these privileges and the effect of all this renders each of the guarantors liable in all respects as principal debtors jointly and severally, which includes the liability to be sued before recourse is had against the debtor.

statement: A lender is not under a duty to advise a borrower on the viability of a transaction or to ensure that the borrower gets good title to the property.
supporting_quote: This is one reason why a borrower is not entitled to rely on the fact that the lender has chosen to lend him the money as evidence, still less as advice, that the lender thinks that the purpose for which the borrower intends to use it is sound.

statement: A creditor must exhaust his legal remedies against the principal debtor for payment right up to the execution against his property before pursuing a surety.
supporting_quote: It means that the creditor must exhaust his legal remedies against the principal debtor for payment right up to the execution against his property [See Grotious 3.3.27; Voet 46.1.14; Van Leeuwen CF 1.4.17.18; Hurley v. Marais (1883) 2 SC 155; Wolfson v. Crowe 1904 TS 682; Worthington v. Wilson 1918 TPD 104].

statement: An action to recover a debt based on an account stated is not prescribed in three years, but in one year if it is based on goods sold and delivered.
supporting_quote: An action to recover the balance was prescribed in three years.

statement: A person who has agreed to purchase a house on an installment basis can use the agreement as proof of residence.
supporting_quote: When considering the totality of the evidence placed before this Court, I hold that the 1st Petitioner is entitled to obtain full marks to the document produce marked as 9A, the main document in proof of the Residence of the Petitioner.

statement: The polluter should, in principle, bear the cost of pollution.
supporting_quote: It is an oft-cited and applied principle of environmental law that the “Polluter Pays”.

statement: A Public Officer must be informed of sufficient details to enable him to exercise his constitutional right of appeal against a transfer order.
supporting_quote: Hence, in order to exercise the constitutional right given to a Public Officer to appeal against a transfer order, he must be made aware of the grounds of the transfer.

statement: A transfer on exigencies of service must be based on one of the three criteria specified in Clause 218, and the officer being transferred must be informed of the reasons behind the transfer.
supporting_quote: The Petitioner who faced the transfer on exigencies of service was deprived of properly defending himself without knowing the real reason for his transfer, when compared to a transfer made on disciplinary grounds, where the officer is well aware of the reason for his transfer.

statement: A public officer's transfer must be based on a valid reason and the officer must be made aware of the reason.
supporting_quote: The PSC Rules recognise three different categories of exigencies of service, so merely stating that it was on exigencies of service is not sufficient.

statement: A person who may be adversely affected by a decision must have an opportunity to make representations on their own behalf before or after the decision is taken, or both.
supporting_quote: Fairness will very often require that a person who may be adversely affected by the decision will have an opportunity to make representations on his own behalf either before the decision is taken with a view to producing a favourable result; or after it is taken with a view to procuring its modification; or both.

statement: An attorney's conduct must be judged in relation to accepted standards of professional propriety and competence.
supporting_quote: Without endeavouring to embark on a precise definition of the word malpractice in section 42(2) of the Judicature Act, it is my view that to warrant the exercise of the disciplinary powers of this court on the ground that an attorney is guilty of malpractice the professional misconduct complained of must be of such a character as, in the opinion of this court, could fairly and reasonably be regarded as being improper or deplorable or reprehensible when judged in relation to the accepted standards of professional propriety and competence.

statement: A practicing attorney-at-law and notary public who has been convicted of serious offenses, including forgery and fraud, and has received a light sentence, may be suspended from practicing his profession for a period of eight years.
supporting_quote: It is unimaginable that the original records and files maintained by the High Court of Colombo and the Attorney General’s Department, which are the primary institutions involved in law enforcement, could be made to disappear so easily.

statement: A notary who is also an Attorney-at-law is expected to maintain high standards and follow the rules and procedure stringently.
supporting_quote: Every notary is expected to carry out a search in the land registry as stipulated in section 31(17) subject to the proviso to the section.
